title: Karnataka Explores Anthropic Partnership to Deploy AI Across Public Services
excerpt: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met Anthropic's international policy head in Bengaluru to discuss AI-driven governance, fraud detection, workforce skilling, and the state's planned AI University.
body:
• Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met a senior Anthropic delegation led by international policy head Michael Sellitto at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru on Thursday.
  • Discussions covered deploying AI for fraud detection in government systems, cybersecurity, secure exam preparation, and citizen-facing public services.
  • The state proposed a Claude certification programme under its NIPUNA skilling initiative and discussed integrating Anthropic's expertise into the planned Karnataka AI University.
  • No formal agreement has been signed, but both sides agreed to continue discussions on AI-led governance and talent development.

Karnataka is in talks with Anthropic, the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence company behind the Claude family of AI models, to deploy the technology across public administration, education, scientific research, and workforce development.

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met a senior Anthropic delegation at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru on Thursday. The meeting included Anthropic's Head of International Policy Michael Sellitto, Karnataka Minister for Electronics, IT/BT and Home Priyank Kharge, Finance Adviser L.K. Atheeq, and other senior state officials, according to YourStory.

AI for Governance and Security

The discussions centred on practical applications of AI in state operations. Karnataka sought Anthropic's expertise in using AI to detect and reduce fraud in government systems — an area where pattern recognition and anomaly detection could significantly cut losses in public spending.

Both sides also explored deploying AI to strengthen cybersecurity infrastructure and improve the delivery of citizen-facing public services. A particularly notable proposal involved using AI to enhance the security, confidentiality, and efficiency of question paper preparation for government examinations — addressing a persistent vulnerability in India's testing system.

"We had a meaningful discussion on the transformative potential of artificial intelligence and explored opportunities to collaborate in areas such as citizen-centric governance, skilling, scientific research, startup enablement and our AI University initiative."

— D.K. Shivakumar, Chief Minister of Karnataka

Skilling and Startup Ecosystem

Karnataka outlined plans to build an AI ecosystem around three pillars: the proposed Karnataka AI University, large-scale skilling programmes, and support for deep-tech innovation. The state discussed creating AI certification programmes with Anthropic, including a potential Claude certification under the NIPUNA initiative — Karnataka's skills development framework.

Healthcare and scientific research were identified as additional collaboration areas. The state also explored ways to support startups developing deep-tech and AI-led solutions, positioning Bengaluru's existing startup ecosystem as a launchpad for AI-native companies.

Enterprise AI and Data Sovereignty

The talks addressed enterprise AI adoption with an emphasis on responsible deployment. Both sides acknowledged data privacy and data sovereignty as critical considerations when handling sensitive government and citizen information — a point of particular importance given India's evolving data protection framework under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.

Shivakumar said the government would work to ensure AI's benefits remain "inclusive, responsible and accessible," adding that Karnataka would "continue to support collaborative initiatives that strengthen Karnataka's innovation ecosystem, creating better public services and greater opportunities for our people."

What It Means for India's AI Landscape

The meeting signals Karnataka's ambition to position itself as India's primary AI governance hub, building on Bengaluru's established dominance in the country's technology sector. If a formal partnership materialises, it would mark one of the first direct collaborations between an Indian state government and a leading frontier AI company.

For the Indian diaspora in tech — many of whom maintain professional and personal ties to Karnataka — the partnership could create new channels for engagement. NRI entrepreneurs and AI researchers have increasingly looked for ways to contribute to India's technology buildout, and a state-level AI initiative with a company of Anthropic's calibre could accelerate those opportunities.

What's Next

No formal agreement or implementation timeline has been announced. Karnataka and Anthropic have agreed to continue discussions on AI-led governance, talent development, research, and innovation. The pace of any partnership will likely depend on the resolution of data sovereignty frameworks and the progress of Karnataka's AI University project, which remains in its planning stages.
